title: The Anatomy — Measured Live, Never Invented

intelligence.essence: The number is built from the Dashboard button anatomy, measured in a real browser from nayanet.app/dashboard (2026-11-07 20:19–20:28Z). Outside to inside: a 1–2px light rim, brightest on the top arc (2px violet #a06bff on featured buttons, 1.5–2px silver-grey on neutral ones) · a black gradient face, top #171720, mid #0f0f15, bottom #020203 — the obsidian black, always visible · a 1px white-grey highlight on the top arc · white bold content, with a soft lavender-grey halo · a soft drop shadow plus a diffused coloured halo outside the rim. The colour lives in the rim, the cap, or a small chip — never on the glyph itself. The number stays white.
intelligence.human_view: Shawn's rule is harvest first: take what already exists and is already beautiful, and build from it. The Dashboard's buttons were already the language. The number just speaks it.
intelligence.child_view: Before you build a new toy, look at the toys you already have. Copy the best parts. Then your new toy fits right in with all the others.
intelligence.grandma_view: You don't invent a new kind of button when the ones you have are already beautiful. You measure the beautiful ones, and you make the new thing the same way.
intelligence.ai_view: Every builder brief names its harvest sources — the exact file, the exact section, the exact line. The design-law gate fails any build whose elements do not trace to the piece index or a named harvest source. The anatomy is the proof: the number traces to the Dashboard, pixel by pixel.
intelligence.what_it_means:
- The number's rim, face, highlight, halo and shadow are the Dashboard's, copied verbatim — not redesigned.
- No gold on the Dashboard components seen. The accent is violet #a06bff, silver-grey, and per-section colours.
- The Hub could not be studied — it hangs (the known feed hang). The Dashboard anatomy is the measured one.
whats_inside:
- Any new element starts from a live measurement of the page it will live on, never from imagination.
- The anatomy is in the build record (HOW-THE-NUMBER-WAS-BUILT.md) and in the Parts Registry, so the next builder measures nothing twice.
